content.value_statement: Healthcare data projects face strict consent, privacy, genetic resource, ownership, and transfer requirements in China. This skill structures risk assessments and practical compliance paths.
actual_capabilities: Classifies clinical, imaging, genetic, monitoring, pharmaceutical, and research data by sensitivity.
Assesses separate consent requirements and outlines consent withdrawal controls.
Screens projects for human genetic resource approval or filing requirements.
Maps patient, hospital, and physician rights and identifies the likely contracting party.
Compares anonymization, explicit authorization, and research pathways for proposed data uses.
Produces structured checklists, remediation actions, and conditional proceed decisions.
limitations: It does not replace advice from a licensed lawyer or approval from a regulator.
Its legal references focus primarily on healthcare data compliance in China.
It cannot verify technical anonymization without detailed methods, samples, and reidentification testing.
Users must confirm current laws, guidance, and agency procedures before implementation.

use_cases.title: Hospital Data Project Review
use_cases.description: Assess planned analytics or assetization against consent, ownership, privacy, ethics, and approval requirements.

use_cases.title: Medical AI Training Assessment
use_cases.description: Compare anonymization and authorization paths for clinical or imaging data used in model training.

use_cases.title: Genetic Research Screening
use_cases.description: Identify human genetic resource controls for collection, collaboration, external provision, and cross-border transfer.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Healthcare Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify these healthcare datasets by type and sensitivity: [datasets]. Explain which items are sensitive personal information and why.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner classification of a known dataset inventory

prompt_templates.title: Check Consent Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed use: [purpose]. Identify separate consent needs, required notices, withdrawal controls, and missing facts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Consent review for a defined processing activity

prompt_templates.title: Design a Compliance Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare anonymization, explicit authorization, and research pathways for [project]. Recommend a path with prerequisites, evidence, owners, and stop conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a healthcare data project

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Gate Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [project] across data sensitivity, consent, ethics, human genetic resources, ownership, sharing, and cross-border transfer. Provide gaps, remediation, and a conditional decision.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before project approval or contracting

output_examples.input: Can deidentified CT images be used to train a diagnostic model?
output: Decision: More information and remediation are required before use.
Confirm whether deidentification prevents reidentification and removes embedded image metadata.
Verify patient authorization, ethics approval, purpose limits, retention, and model partner access.
Treat the images as sensitive personal information unless true anonymization is demonstrated.

output_examples.input: A hospital plans to provide genetic data to an overseas research partner.
output: Decision: Stop external provision until regulatory screening is complete.
Confirm whether the data qualifies as human genetic resource information.
Document consent, ethics review, collaboration structure, recipient, purpose, and transfer route.
Obtain specialist legal review and confirm current approval, filing, and transfer requirements.

output_examples.input: Who should sign a contract for a hospital data analytics project?
output_examples.output: The hospital is usually the contracting data controller, but the authorization chain must cover the proposed purpose. Confirm patient rights and physician-related issues.

best_practices: Provide the data inventory, processing purpose, recipients, locations, retention period, and current consent evidence.
Separate anonymization from deidentification and document reidentification risk testing.
Confirm current requirements with legal counsel, ethics bodies, and regulators before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not assume deidentified data is anonymous or outside personal information rules.
Do not reuse broad privacy notices as separate consent for unrelated sensitive data processing.
Do not share genetic or medical data externally before completing approval and transfer screening.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured compliance analysis and planning support, not a licensed legal opinion.

faq.question: Which jurisdiction does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on healthcare data requirements in China. Other jurisdictions require separate analysis.

faq.question: Can it decide whether data is truly anonymous?
faq.answer: It can review stated methods and risks. Technical validation requires detailed testing and qualified security review.

faq.question: Does every healthcare project require separate consent?
faq.answer: Not always. The answer depends on data type, legal basis, purpose, anonymization, research context, and applicable exceptions.

faq.question: Can it review human genetic resource issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It can screen likely approval or filing needs, but current agency procedures require independent confirmation.

faq.question: What information produces the best assessment?
faq.answer: Provide data types, subjects, purpose, recipients, transfer locations, retention, security controls, consent records, and research approvals.
